title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
hook: Attention lets a model decide which parts of the input to focus on. Scaled dot-product attention computes similarity between queries and keys, turns those similarities into weights, and uses them to mix values. This page lets you edit Q, K, and V and see exactly how the output is built.

symbols.meaning: Query matrix: one row per query, one column per feature.
Key matrix: one row per key, one column per feature.
Value matrix: one row per key, one column per output feature.
Number of columns in Q and K (feature dimension).
Raw similarity scores: S = Q K^T.
Attention weights after softmax, one row per query.
Output matrix: weighted sum of V rows.

steps.explain: Compute similarity between each query and each key.
Scale down scores so softmax does not saturate.
Turn each row of scores into a probability distribution.
Each output row is a weighted average of the value rows.

explorations.title: Equal scores give uniform attention
explorations.predict: If all keys are identical, what will each row of A look like?
explorations.why: When all scores in a row are equal, softmax gives equal weights.

explorations.title: Dominant score focuses attention
explorations.predict: If one key is much more similar to the query, what happens to its weight?
explorations.observe: The first weight is close to 1, the second close to 0.
explorations.why: A much larger score dominates the softmax.

limitation: This page shows one attention head on tiny matrices. Real Transformers use many heads, multiple layers, and much larger dimensions.
misconception: Attention weights are not the same as the output. The output is a weighted sum of the value rows, so it can be different from the weights.

claims.text: Scaled dot-product attention computes softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V.
Each row of the attention weight matrix sums to 1.
The output is a weighted sum of the value rows.

selftests.why: Softmax always produces rows that sum to 1.
Output equals the weighted sum of V rows.
With scaling off, scaled scores equal raw scores.
